12.text: Musk said the SpaceX-Tesla-Intel chip fab Terafab targets volume production in 2028, though an analyst expects significant output nearer 2030; it is reportedly courting about 10 Korean suppliers. Musk also claimed the single Texas building would rank in the top 20 of national GDP.

6.text: Rivian reached No. 2 in U.S. EV registrations in August, with Amazon van sales up 87% year-over-year. Global EV and battery-reuse markets are projected to grow sharply, European registrations rose 10% in September, and Tesla appears mainly via a Roadster mention.

7.text: Tesla beat Q3 estimates with $0.48 adjusted EPS on $28.0B revenue, but automotive revenue fell 3%, energy storage dropped 16%, and operating income declined 56% with margins at 2.6%. Shares slipped on delivery declines and profit-quality concerns, though free cash flow turned positive.

5.text: SpaceX beat Q3 estimates with $14.58B revenue and its first profit, sending shares up roughly 8-10%. Musk and both boards are now studying a Tesla-SpaceX merger, which analysts call the biggest-ever deal.

4.text: Tesla plans to sell Cybercabs to customers by end-2026, with most owned by Tesla itself, and aims to launch in Dallas next month while expanding its Austin fleet tenfold. Quarterly profit fell 43% to $787 million amid robot and self-driving spending, and Latvia approved Full Self-Driving (Supervised).

15.text: Elon Musk reportedly invested $1 billion in Skydance, with panelists discussing the timing of the move. The article does not otherwise bear directly on Tesla.

19.text: Tesla unveiled a second-generation Roadster with cold-gas thrusters and suction technology on October 15, 2026, though the flying version won't be available to the general public initially. With Tesla shares under pressure, Elon Musk is promoting the flying Roadster as a way to lift the stock.

8.text: Tesla began volume production of its Semi truck, reported 72.5% September registration growth in Europe, and dropped Cybertruck plans for Australia and New Zealand. Musk said demand exceeds production and set a goal of 5 million vehicles annually by 2030, while Tesla pursues AI mapping and a $2.8 billion AI component investment.

18.text: Samsung Electro-Mechanics will expand FC-BGA substrate manufacturing under a Won4.27tn capex programme that includes a planned Won1.1tn Tesla investment. Nvidia also backs the expansion.
